correctness.rationale: For k≥2, Menon–Singh Lemma 3.6 gives B_{ℓ+1,p}(k) equal to the number of runs of length k−1, so a strongly equivalent q must have identical run-length multiset and number of runs. For p=1^a0^b1^c and n=ℓ+2, expand ∑_{host}X_p(host)^2 as ordered pairs of embeddings specified by deleted two-element sets A,B. If A=B, weight four; if |A∩B|=1, weight two and compatible distinct omission positions occur within the same constant run; if disjoint, the six A/B labellings of four positions admit exactly 2U+4V placements with the stated formulas. This yields a symmetric sum minus 2ac·1_{b≥2}. For fixed multiset, this zero-or-negative term identifies b=1 uniquely if present, else its magnitude 2abc/b identifies the middle run. The outer run order is reversal and the first bit is complement. Independently generated all 2^(ℓ+2) hosts and computed embedding counts by dynamic programming for 54 distinct positive triples with a,b,c≤4 and ℓ≤9, all matching the exact formula; independently classified all six disjoint-hole shapes for 125 triples a,b,c≤5, matching the two U and four V counts. The example is 598/592/594 for different middle runs. Infinite correctness follows from six-shape combinatorial classification rather than finite tests.

originality.rationale: Menon–Singh precisely conjectured that reversal/complement are the only strong Wilf equivalences and verified only length≤13; their different at-most-three-run theorems concern maximal occurrence counts and internal zeros, not this all-length classification. Tian develops occurrence-computation algorithms and primitive binary words without resolving the conjecture. No equivalence/dominating theorem was found in Resultary. The finite small-host second moment supplies a new separating invariant.
residual_risks: A stronger recent or unindexed Wilf-equivalence classification could subsume this three-run case; no global literature-completeness guarantee is supplied.
The six-shape disjoint-hole classification needs its explicit combinatorial boundary argument; finite DP checks only corroborate that lemma.

final_claim: Binary subsequence patterns with at most three runs are strongly Wilf-equivalent to arbitrary patterns only under reversal and/or bit complement. The run multiset is recovered at host length ℓ+1; an exact sum of squared occurrence counts at host length ℓ+2 distinguishes the middle run and proves Menon–Singh Conjecture 5.2 in this infinite class.
limitations: Exactly binary scattered subsequences, at most three runs; no claim for four or more runs or larger alphabets.
Raw summed second moment at host length ℓ+2, not normalized variance.
